correctness.rationale: Fractional matching vertices are disjoint unit edges and vertex-disjoint half-valued odd cycles. For a uniform near-perfect matching on each odd cycle length ℓ, exact independent rational calculation verifies gain w_e[(ℓ−2)/(4ℓ)+c_e/ℓ]>0 for c_e≥0 (checked ℓ=3,5,7,9 and c=0,1/4,3/2). Thus no fractional extreme vertex maximizes squared distance, and strict convexity excludes other nonmatching boundary points. Clamping proposed centers to nonnegative proves identical minimax ball center/radius; midpoint identity ensures unique center. Farthest-point replacement twice yields equal diameters and integral diametral endpoints. All finite G, positive diagonal metric; no claim for negative c or non-diagonal metric.

value.rationale: Nontrivial structural invariance of *two* ambient Euclidean metrics of fractional vs integral matching polytopes for all finite graphs and arbitrary diagonal weights; quantitative strict vertex slack identifies contact points and a graph-theoretic diameter formula. Not merely the known half-integral vertex theorem.

final_claim: For all finite loopless graphs, positive diagonal edge weights and nonnegative center c, squared Euclidean farthest distances over fractional and integral matching polytopes coincide, every fractional vertex has strict gap, and both polytopes share minimum weighted enclosing ball and Euclidean diameter.
limitations: No statement for nonpositive diagonal weights, signed pointwise centers, or off-diagonal quadratic metrics.
Broader unnamed separable convex-matching extremal theorem might cover the result.
